skill.name: troubleshoot
skill.description: Guides structured troubleshooting for code projects when errors or broken behavior appear.
skill.summary: Diagnoses code, build, dependency, Git, UI, and LSP problems with guided checks.
skill.author: Chachamaru127

security_audit.summary: The skill is mostly troubleshooting guidance, and many backtick findings are markdown false positives. Confirmed risks remain where it directs npm, git, build, and test execution, especially an automatic npm install flow without clear confirmation.

remediation.issue: Automatic package-manager actions are recommended in troubleshooting examples.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before npm install, npm run build, npm test, cache clearing, or reinstalling node_modules.

remediation.issue: Diagnostic commands can run project-defined scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer read-only checks first, explain side effects, and isolate package-script execution behind a confirmation step.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples use broad code fences that triggered static command detections.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as illustrative text and separate executable commands from sample output and prose.

content.value_statement: Broken builds, blank screens, and dependency errors slow project work. This skill guides structured diagnosis, evidence collection, fixes, and escalation.
actual_capabilities: Classifies dependency, type, build, runtime, environment, Git, and UI failure symptoms.
Suggests Node, npm, Git, build, test, and dependency health checks.
Guides UI issue reproduction with browser, console, network, and source evidence.
Uses LSP diagnostics and go-to-definition workflows to trace likely causes.
Provides escalation report patterns after repeated failed fixes.
limitations: Focuses on Node and npm projects, so other stacks may need adaptation.
Package-manager, build, test, and Git actions need user review before execution.
Root-cause quality depends on logs, reproduction steps, and current project state.
Browser and LSP workflows require compatible tools outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Recover From a Broken App
use_cases.description: Collect symptoms, identify likely categories, and receive a simple repair path for common project failures.

use_cases.title: Debug Frontend Behavior
use_cases.description: Reproduce UI bugs, inspect console or network evidence, and connect symptoms to source files.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Escalation Report
use_cases.description: Summarize errors, attempted fixes, and likely causes when repeated troubleshooting does not resolve the issue.

prompt_templates.title: Start Basic Diagnosis
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a broken project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this project problem. The app is not working, and I need a simple explanation of the likely cause and next step.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Blank Screen
prompt_templates.scenario: UI loads but shows no useful content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose why the page is blank. Check likely build, runtime, routing, and browser console causes before suggesting a fix.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an npm Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Dependency installation or build command fails.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this npm or dependency failure. Explain the probable cause, side effects of each fix, and ask before running package commands.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Troubleshooting Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced escalation after several failed repair attempts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an escalation report with symptoms, evidence, commands reviewed, fixes attempted, remaining hypotheses, and the safest next actions.

output_examples.input: The screen is blank after the latest change.
output_examples.output: A concise diagnosis lists likely runtime, routing, or build causes, then asks for console evidence before recommending a fix.

output_examples.input: npm install fails with a dependency conflict.
output_examples.output: The response explains the dependency conflict, separates safe checks from modifying actions, and requests approval before changing dependencies.

output_examples.input: The same error returns after three repair attempts.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares a shareable report with the error summary, attempted fixes, suspected root cause, and escalation notes.

best_practices: Provide the exact symptom, recent change, and expected behavior before diagnosis starts.
Review any package-manager, build, test, Git, or file-changing action before approval.
Keep logs and reproduction steps attached to each troubleshooting attempt.
anti_patterns: Running dependency or Git fixes without reading the proposed side effects.
Treating sample output as proof that the same cause exists in your project.
Skipping escalation after repeated failed automatic repair attempts.

faq.question: What problems does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets broken apps, build errors, dependency failures, Git issues, UI bugs, and LSP-detected code problems.

faq.question: Does it work only with Claude?
faq.answer: No. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Will it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It may suggest commands. Review and approve package, build, test, Git, and file-changing actions before execution.

faq.question: Can it fix dependency conflicts?
faq.answer: It can explain likely causes and suggest repair steps, but dependency changes should be confirmed by the user.

faq.question: Can it diagnose UI bugs?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides reproduction, browser evidence collection, source review, and verification after a fix.

faq.question: What happens if the issue remains unresolved?
faq.answer: It guides creation of an escalation report with evidence, attempted fixes, and likely causes.
